title: Heliostat clinical-recs warmstart vs steady-state latency insights
content:
Summary:
This note captures experiments and operational observations from the Heliostat clinical-recommendations POC focused on tail-latency behavior during two operational modes: warmstart (pre-warmed KV cache + persistent model workers) and steady-state (long-running service after sustained load). Goal: quantify p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, sustainable QPS, and token-level cost for combinations of model variants and runtime configurations, then recommend a production-ready deployment pattern that meets the customer SLA of p95 <= 250ms for single-turn recommendation queries while also minimizing cost growth under bursty traffic.

Context and workload profile:
- Workload: single-turn clinical recommendation queries (avg prompt length ~120 tokens, output ~60 tokens). Many queries reuse similar prefixes (patient metadata blobs) so KV prefix caching is expected to be effective.
- Expected traffic: baseline 120 QPS with occasional microbursts up to 1.2k QPS for 30-90s.
- Quality target: model-ranked top-3 suggestions must match a clinical rubric; primary experiments used two model candidates: HelioBase-13B (FP16) and HelioCore-70B-int8 (aggressively quantized).
- Hardware tested: H100-80GB (dedicated), A100-80GB (dedicated), and shared-hosted pool of mixed A10G for cost-comparison.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Mode A: warmstart, persistent workers pinned, KV cache prefilled from a synthetic primer run; batching window set to 6ms.
- Mode B: steady-state, warmup from cold but after 30m steady load; KV cache populated organically.
- Config variants: batching disabled vs batching=6ms vs batching=12ms; admission control present vs absent; fallback routing enabled (70B -> 13B) vs disabled.

Key observational results (aggregated):
- HelioBase-13B on H100 (warmstart, batching=6ms): p50=48ms, p90=92ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms; sustained QPS = 480 (single GPU, continuous). Cost baseline: ~$0.45 per 10k tokens served (including infra amortized).
- HelioBase-13B on H100 (steady-state, batching=6ms): p50=60ms, p90=130ms, p95=185ms, p99=320ms; observed microburst tail amplification (p99 doubled) on sudden ramp if KV cache not primed.
- HelioCore-70B-int8 on H100 (warmstart): p50=95ms, p90=190ms, p95=260ms, p99=420ms; sustained QPS = 260; cost: ~$1.10 per 10k tokens. Quality uplift vs 13B was marginal for our rubric (~3% stat sig) but not clearly worth the 2.4x cost.
- On A100-80GB numbers were ~12-18% slower at tail compared to H100 for equivalent configs. Mixed-hosted A10G pool showed great cost but inconsistent p99 behavior under burst.

Warmstart vs Steady-state notes: 
- Warmstart advantages were highest for p95/p99 during first 60s of a burst due to KV prefix hits and warmed CUDA kernel caches. Prefilling KV with the top 500 common prefixes (derived from production traces) reduced p95 by ~45% in the first minute of a ramp.
- Steady-state after >10 minutes of load converged to slightly higher median latency but similar p90; however p99 remained sensitive to microbursts unless admission control or small LRU cache was used.
- Cold-start to steady-state (no prewarming) had up to 3x p99 increases during the first 90s of a large ramp.

Batching and admission control trade-offs:
- Batching=6ms gave best cost-to-latency ratio for HelioBase-13B at target QPS: added ~12% latency on p50 but reduced per-token compute cost by ~18% due to better GPU utilization.
- Batching=12ms produced slightly better cost but pushes p95 over SLA during bursts.
- Admission control (reject or queue with graceful degradation) dramatically reduced p99 spikes: when QPS > burst threshold, queueing + fast-fail to smaller model kept p95 under control.

KV cache observations and heuristics:
- Prefix-based KV cache (patient header tokens): priming top-500 prefixes reduced initial-burst p95 by 30-50% depending on model size.
- Cache eviction tuned to LRU with TTL 15m worked well; too-long TTL (60m) grew memory pressure and produced cache thrash on memory-constrained GPUs.

Cost sensitivity summary (example numbers normalized to HelioBase-13B warmstart on H100):
- Baseline: 1 H100 serving HelioBase-13B at 480 QPS sustained -> cost X (reference).
- Switching to HelioCore-70B-int8 -> cost ~2.4X for similar coverage; better quality margin not decisive for clinical-rubric.
- Shared-hosted mixed GPUs -> cost 0.6X but p99 variance increases; recommended only for non-critical lanes or canary traffic.

Deployment recommendation for Heliostat POC (concise):
1) Primary: Dedicated H100 pool running HelioBase-13B, persistent workers, batching=6ms, KV prefix cache primed with top-500 prefixes, admission control threshold at 600 QPS per GPU equivalent with fast-fail to 13B -> 13B is both primary and fallback depending on config; if HelioCore-70B is mandatory for quality, run it only for canary cohorts.
2) Canary/Cost lanes: hosted mixed GPUs with smaller models for exploratory traffic only.
3) Autoscale policy: aggressive horizontal scaling + pre-warming step on new nodes to apply KV primes before accepting traffic; prefer warmboot vs cold-launch for planned increases.
4) Monitoring: per-route p95, cache hit-rate, effective batch size, and eviction rate; alert if p95 > 200ms or cache hit-rate drops below 65% during steady-state.

Operational runbook snippets:
- Pre-burst checklist: verify KV prime snapshot uploaded to /kv-primes/heliostat/top500, compare checksum, increment canary by 5% before full ramp.
- On spike: enable admission control -> queue up to 100ms else fast-fail to smaller model; if p99 continues to climb, reduce batch window from 6ms to 3ms temporarily.

Unresolved questions and next experiments:
- Run a longitudinal 48h mixed-workload test to measure cache pollution effects (we only ran 4h windows).
- Evaluate intermediate model sizes (30B) and 4-bit quantization trade-offs; early tests suggested 30B-int4 may approach 70B-int8 quality at 60% cost.
- Validate medical-rubric drift under fallback routing (does fallback harm final ranking consistency?).

Appendix (short):
- Raw measurement artifacts: S3 logs at s3://redwood-logs/heliostat/poc/warmstart-2028-09/*.jsonl
- Key tickets: SE-2345 (end-to-end POC plan), SE-2360 (autoscale + warmboot PR), PR #812 in serving-runtime adjust batching policy.

Concluding note:
For this clinical-recs workload, the 13B class model on dedicated H100s with KV priming and modest batching hits the customer p95 <= 250ms SLA while keeping token cost moderate. The larger 70B-int8 model improves some rubric metrics but at materially higher cost and worse tail latency; recommend reserving it for small cohorts or offline re-rank.

- Maya
